newsitem.title: JAPAN: North Korea says it, U.S. to exhume war remains.
newsitem.headline: North Korea says it, U.S. to exhume war remains.

text.p: North Korea said on Monday that starting next month it and the United States will conduct three joint exhumations of remains of U.S. soldiers who went missing in action during the 1950-53 Korean War.
Pyongyang's official Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) said working-level bilateral talks on the exhumations took place in New York from June 25 to 27 based on an agreement reached in May.
"They agreed to conduct three rounds of joint exhumation in Unsan county, North Phyongan province, in July, September and October," KCNA said in the report, which was monitored in Tokyo.
Washington said in May that the United States had agreed to pay $105,500 in expenses for each of three joint searches for U.S. remains.
There are 8,100 U.S. troops still listed as missing in the Korean War.
